nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift and splice variants, including the East Asian founder c.796C>T (p.Arg266*) and a Chinese deep intronic founder variant that inserts a pseudo-exon, all truncate SERPINB7 before its reactive site.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: We identified a major causative mutation of c.796C>T (p.Arg266(∗)) as a founder mutation in Japanese and Chinese populations.

evidence.reference_title: A deep intronic founder variant in the SERPINB7 gene causing aberrant splicing is a potential therapeutic target for Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: A deep intronic SERPINB7 variant was identified in six NPPK patients, leading to pseudo-exon inclusion and the production of a truncated, dysfunctional SERPINB7 protein.

nodes.description: Mild, diffuse, well-demarcated hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles that extends onto the dorsal fingers and toes, the inner wrists, the Achilles tendon area, knees and elbows, while the central backs of the hands stay clear.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: "Nagashima-type" palmoplantar keratosis (NPPK) is an autosomal recessive nonsyndromic diffuse palmoplantar keratosis characterized by well-demarcated diffuse hyperkeratosis with redness, expanding on to the dorsal surfaces of the palms and feet and the Achilles tendon area.

evidence.reference_title: History and prospects of Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis, the most common palmoplantar keratoderma in east Asian populations.
evidence.snippet: The redness extends to the dorsal surface of the toes, fingers, and the Achilles tendon areas (transgrediens), while the central dorsal area of the hands remains unaffected.

nodes.description: The stratum corneum lets water in and out too easily. In patients, water exposure turns lesional skin white and spongy within minutes; in knockout mice, the barrier is spontaneously disrupted.

animal_models.description: The knockout reproduces the barrier defect.
animal_models.name: Serpinb7-null mouse

animal_models.description: Shows the barrier defect is keratinocyte-intrinsic.
animal_models.name: Keratinocyte-specific Serpinb7 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: SERPINB7 Deficiency Increases Legumain Activity and Impairs the Epidermal Barrier in Nagashima-Type Palmoplantar Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: In this study, Serpinb7-/- mice were generated and spontaneously developed a disrupted skin barrier, which was further exacerbated by acetone-ether-water treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: Before water exposure, the mean TEWL values were higher in the lesional skin of NPPK individuals than in the nonlesional skin of NPPK individuals or the corresponding skin area of normal healthy controls (Figure 4B)

nodes.description: A distinctive plantar odor that impairs quality of life.

evidence.reference_title: Microbial dysbiosis and foot odor in Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis: Improvement with topical benzoyl peroxide.
evidence.snippet: It is characterized by erythematous hyperkeratosis, palmoplantar hyperhidrosis, and a distinctive foot odor that significantly impairs QOL.

nodes.description: SERPINB7-deficient keratinocytes lose Golgi structure and O-GalNAc glycosyltransferases, so calcium-related and adhesion proteins are under-glycosylated.

evidence.reference_title: SERPINB7 maintains skin barrier by regulating protein O-GalNAc glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: SERPINB7 deficiency leads to reduced expression of O-GalNAc regulatory proteins and structural abnormalities in the Golgi apparatus, ultimately impairing protein O-GalNAc glycosylation.

experimental_models.description: Knockdown reproduces the Golgi and glycosylation defect, rescued by legumain knockdown.
experimental_models.name: SERPINB7-silenced human keratinocytes

nodes.description: Tight junctions between keratinocytes are lost, with less occludin and weaker cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion.

evidence.reference_title: SERPINB7 maintains skin barrier by regulating protein O-GalNAc glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: We found that SERPINB7 deficiency disrupts tight junctions of keratinocytes in vitro, and specific knockout of Serpinb7 in keratinocytes impairs skin barrier function in vivo.

nodes.description: Mice lacking Serpinb7 in keratinocytes show cracks and fissures and raised transepidermal water loss in dorsal skin, reversed by a topical legumain inhibitor.
Legumain, an asparaginyl endopeptidase, is overactive in SERPINB7-deficient epidermis.

animal_models.description: Legumain activity is increased in knockout skin.
animal_models.name: Serpinb7-null mouse

evidence.reference_title: SERPINB7 Deficiency Increases Legumain Activity and Impairs the Epidermal Barrier in Nagashima-Type Palmoplantar Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Loss of SERPINB7 function led to overactivation of legumain, which might disrupt cytoskeletal proteins, contributing to the impaired skin barrier in Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratoderma.

nodes.description: SERPINB7 is expressed in the cytoplasm of the stratum granulosum and stratum corneum. Despite its family name it behaves as a cysteine protease inhibitor, and its main target is legumain, which it binds and inhibits in a protease-substrate manner.

evidence.reference_title: SERPINB7 Deficiency Increases Legumain Activity and Impairs the Epidermal Barrier in Nagashima-Type Palmoplantar Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Overall, we found that SERPINB7 showed the nature of a cysteine protease inhibitor and identified legumain as a key target protease of SERPINB7.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: SERPINB7 was specifically present in the cytoplasm of the stratum granulosum and the stratum corneum (SC) of the epidermis.

nodes.description: Sole skin carries a higher bacterial load and lower diversity than in healthy controls, dominated by Corynebacterium and Staphylococcus, especially between the toes. What causes the dysbiosis is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Microbial dysbiosis and foot odor in Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis: Improvement with topical benzoyl peroxide.
evidence.snippet: Compared with healthy controls, individuals with Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis exhibited significantly higher objective odor scores; increased bacterial load, especially in the intertoe area; and reduced microbial diversity.

nodes.description: SERPINB7 loss lowers keratinocyte differentiation in a three-dimensional human epidermal model.

evidence.reference_title: SERPINB7 Deficiency Increases Legumain Activity and Impairs the Epidermal Barrier in Nagashima-Type Palmoplantar Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: In addition, SERPINB7 deficiency consistently led to decreased epidermal differentiation in a 3-dimensional human epidermal model.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: showed no major keratinocyte differentiation defect in NPPK skin (Figure 3E).

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: We performed whole-exome and/or Sanger sequencing analyses of 13 unrelated NPPK individuals and identified biallelic putative loss-of-function mutations in SERPINB7, which encodes a cytoplasmic member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily.

evidence.reference_title: Large-Scale Cohort Study on the Genetic and Phenotypic Findings of Palmoplantar Keratodermas in the Chinese Population.
evidence.snippet: In 80% (304/380) patients, hotspot variants in SERPINB7 were identified, with c.796C>T (77%) and c.522_523insT (16%) being the most frequent.

nodes.description: Second most frequent hotspot variant in Chinese patients.

evidence.snippet: In 80% (304/380) patients, hotspot variants in SERPINB7 were identified, with c.796C>T (77%) and c.522_523insT (16%) being the most frequent.

nodes.description: East Asian founder variant, the most frequent NPPK allele in Japan and China.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SERPINB7, encoding a member of the serine protease inhibitor superfamily, cause Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis.
evidence.snippet: We identified a major causative mutation of c.796C>T (p.Arg266(∗)) as a founder mutation in Japanese and Chinese populations.

nodes.description: HaCaT cells and primary neonatal human epidermal keratinocytes with SERPINB7 knocked down by siRNA.
Global Serpinb7 knockout mice develop a disrupted skin barrier, worsened by acetone-ether-water challenge, with weakened cytoskeletal proteins and increased legumain activity.
Topical benzoyl peroxide to the feet reduces foot odor and bacterial load and restores microbial diversity.

evidence.reference_title: Microbial dysbiosis and foot odor in Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis: Improvement with topical benzoyl peroxide.
evidence.snippet: The topical application of benzoyl peroxide significantly reduced foot odor and bacterial load; increased microbial diversity; and selectively decreased Corynebacterium abundance, particularly that of C tuberculostearicum.

nodes.description: Aminoglycoside ointment applied to palms and soles, intended to make ribosomes read through premature stop codons such as p.Arg266* and restore full-length SERPINB7. In a double-blind, vehicle-controlled half-side study it improved hyperkeratosis, desquamation and quality of life but not erythema. In an open-label pediatric half-side study it also improved erythema and maceration, but not hyperhidrosis or odor.

evidence.reference_title: Effect of Gentamicin Ointment in Patients with Nagashima-type Palmoplantar Keratosis: A Double-blind Vehicle-controlled Study.
evidence.snippet: Compared with the control vehicle, gentamicin ointment significantly improved hyperkeratosis, desquamation, and quality of life, based on VAS and DLQI scores.

evidence.reference_title: Effect of Gentamicin Ointment in Patients with Nagashima-type Palmoplantar Keratosis: A Double-blind Vehicle-controlled Study.
evidence.snippet: No difference was found in the effect on erythema between gentamicin and vehicle.

evidence.reference_title: Application of topical gentamicin ointment in the treatment of Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis in children with a nonsense mutation.
evidence.snippet: Bilateral comparisons showed that gentamicin ointment significantly improved hyperkeratosis, erythema, maceration, and desquamation, but not hyperhidrosis and odor, indicating that gentamicin ointment is a promising therapeutic option for children with NPPK.

evidence.snippet: The skin of these Serpinb7-/- mice showed weakened cytoskeletal proteins.

nodes.description: The "water sign": lesional skin turns white and spongy shortly after contact with water and returns to normal when dry. It was seen in all 13 patients of the original series and is considered a diagnostic hallmark.

evidence.reference_title: History and prospects of Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis, the most common palmoplantar keratoderma in east Asian populations.
evidence.snippet: observed that the area of the skin exhibiting erythema and mild hyperkeratosis displayed a whitish change shortly after exposure to water and subsequently reverted to its original state upon drying in all 13 affected individuals.

evidence.reference_title: History and prospects of Nagashima-type palmoplantar keratosis, the most common palmoplantar keratoderma in east Asian populations.
evidence.snippet: This phenomenon, which we term the “water sign,” is a diagnostic hallmark of NPPK (Figure 4) as it has been observed by the majority of parents of infant patients after exposure to water following bathing and swimming.
